The Port St. Lucie Police Department is searching for Johnley Cadet, who was last seen Sunday at a Jimmy John's in Fort Pierce. Police said Cadet was diagnosed with a mental health illness.

Cadet was last seen wearing a white T-shirt, black shorts, and black shoes. He stands about 5 feet 9 inches tall, weighs 185 pounds, and has a tattoo on his right arm that reads Boo and Tinkerbell.

Anyone with information about his whereabouts is asked to call 911 immediately.

hero.body:
The Fort Pierce City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney while the city searches for a permanent replacement. The appointment comes after the commission decided not to renew City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract, Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman resigned, and temporary attorney Caroline Valentin is set to leave at the end of the month.

Commissioner Michael Broderick voted against the appointment and raised concerns about the timing of the legal department shakeup. He said several volatile development projects are expected to come before the commission soon, and the city lacks independent legal representation to handle them. Broderick pointed specifically to future development proposals on South Hutchinson Island and potential changes to the South Beach Overlay, a zoning regulation that currently limits building heights and density. Removing those restrictions could clear the way for much taller development on the island.

Wallace previously worked in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager. Supporters of her appointment said her legal background and familiarity with city operations provide continuity while the city loses much of its legal staff. Broderick criticized the move, saying the city appointed the assistant city manager to serve as a charter officer. He questioned how someone can report to multiple bosses.

The commission approved a contract with executive search firm S. Rene Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney. The agreement authorizes up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. City officials expect the interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution. The search for a permanent city attorney is expected to continue over the coming months.

hero.body:
Fort Pierce's City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney after City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract was not renewed, Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman resigned, and temporary attorney Caroline Valentin is set to leave at the end of the month. The sudden departure of nearly the entire legal department comes as the city prepares to navigate several high-profile development proposals on South Hutchinson Island, including potential changes to the South Beach Overlay that could allow taller buildings and higher density.

Commissioner Michael Broderick voted against Wallace's appointment and said the timing raises concerns about the city's legal representation. "There are several very volatile projects that are slated to come in front of the city commission in short order, and we really have no independent legal representation to be able to deal with that on behalf of the city commission, in my opinion," Broderick told CBS12 News. He added that the South Beach Overlay, a zoning regulation currently limiting building heights and density, could be removed to clear the way for much taller development on the island.

Broderick also objected to the structure of Wallace's dual role. "So what the city commission did against my protests is they appointed the assistant city manager to now be a charter officer in the city of Fort Pierce," Broderick said. "In my opinion, that reeks of duplicity and multiple bosses you need to report to. I'm not sure how that is even possible to do."

Supporters of the appointment said Wallace's previous experience in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager makes her qualified to provide continuity while a permanent replacement is found. The commission approved a contract with executive search firm S. Renée Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney, authorizing up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. City officials expect Wallace's interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution.
